368.t: Manager Lenny Lewis, a brilliant and irritating character
368.s: Lewis raised money for the band but clashed with DeFranco and had been chased off by Artie Shaw.
368.q: No, the group. I reformed the group, I don’t think I reformed the big band; I’m not sure which came. I know I did, I was back and forth, I had a big band and recorded that and also decided to get involved with a jazz group, which was a good move.

368.t: How Lenny Lewis raised money and took half the take
368.s: Lewis got backers including a wealthy woman and Ross Hastings, and kept half of the income.
368.q: I don’t know, in those days, maybe twenty grand or something like that; fifteen thousand, or something. That was a lot of money. Then there was another, he got another guy to put up money, Ross Hastings, whose family was the originator of Formica, he put a, Lenny got him to put up a lot of money in…

259.t: Bob Lyons, his crooked band and its members
259.s: He describes bandleader Bob Lyons as crooked with money, lists sidemen (Bonnie Pigar, Charlie Decanje, Bill Matthews) and a big trombonist who lost both legs.
259.ch: Bob Lyons band and New Orleans musicians
259.q: He said he wants you to talk some more about Bob Lyons. Oh, Bob Lyons? Yeah. Yeah, Bob he said, plenty of kid bands, you know. And, but he was like that crooked. He was like that crooked. Yeah. Yeah. Bob was taking money on the job, you know. And then when we go on the job, you know, we had to come…

626.t: Serving as band secretary and keeping the job record book
626.s: He was appointed secretary and kept a book of jobs, pay and where they played, which settled arguments.
626.q: And, uh, when I joined it, uh, they, they kind of appointed me as secretary, and I kept a record of the, of the jobs we'd play, and what we got out the job, and what each man received, and so on. And, uh, I was, I was the only one, however, with the secretary that locked things down, you see, the…

642.t: Complaint about a tuba-playing leader who controls the money
642.s: Guesnon says phonies who control the money get into the spotlight and cannot be pushed out, using a tuba player as the example.
642.q: It's pretty fair, I mean. Yeah? I mean, it's not the George Lewis record. No, no, no, no. I can't see why he should be there with us. Well, I mean, you know, he's cutting in on everything. Like, I'm telling you, why hire a tuba player and pay him two, three, four hundred dollars, when I can come…

849.t: Closing: paying his men on time
849.s: Asked to add anything, he says he pays musicians before the job, unlike another bandleader, and gets along with them.
849.ch: A difficult club job and closing
849.q: I'm one of the best in the line of music. Get one of the best jobs in the line of music. I get the best. And I'm one of the best paying off in the music, the music ranking with all my mans. I'm one of your best paying off. And then boys, got a good word to say to pay off all my jobs. Some of them…

986.t: Not a good businessman; diva behavior pays
986.s: He never asks for enough money and notes difficult musicians seem to get paid more and become part of jazz folklore.
986.q: No. Not at all. And my wife reminds me of that every day. I’m not a good businessman. I never ask for enough money. I never fight as hard as I should for things. And I don’t demand enough. I’m not a “diva” guy. And it’s funny because in this business you see a lot of musicians, because we play the…

378.s: Whiteman collected $1,500 a week from Paramount for her but paid her little, and when she asked for more she left with a reputation for being temperamental.
378.q: Under certain conditions. I think that's the difference between a lot of people. But I think -- well I think Mildred got a lot of bad publicity when she left Whiteman, saying that she was temperamental.

231.t: Certifying the check and opening the Dunbar Bank account
231.s: Buck sided with Nazarro; Bubbles got the check certified and opened a Buck and Bubbles account, but the bank froze him out, and he still has the checkbook.
231.q: So what happened is that when I don't give him the check, Buck now don't want to do as I'm saying, he want to do what Nazarro is saying and I'm mad at him, I'm ready to kill him. He don't know it but finally they subsided. He told Buck, "He's taken your money he's going to spend it so-and-so-and…

76.t: Marge's account books and Nick's back pay
76.s: When Nick owed the band months of pay, Marge came with her ledgers and collected, impressing Nick. Zutty says that is why she is with him.
76.ch: Theaters, the Navy and the Singletons' partnership
76.q: And I was always making out all the contracts and everything. Well like Nick, Nick hadn't paid them for months down there. He just give them ten dollars a week or something like that. Business was bad, but I had my books that I kept how much he owed Zutty and the band you know. And finally, business
